note: The texture layer (phase 37). Minor incidents composed at tick time from these templates: era-ranged, state-gated via `needs`, weighted, cooled down per template (cooldowns in play minutes, converted at era cadence) so a century never repeats a surface string. This layer IS the m-magnitude tier — authored data keeps W/M/R, and 173 hours of deep past cannot run on authored events alone (07-timeline §5.3).

texts: The rains fail at {place}. The tanks hold, barely.
A second dry year around {place}; the herds are driven further than anyone likes.
The wells at {place} are deepened by hand. The river is a memory this season.
A heavy harvest around {place}. The granaries want repair before winter.
Two good rains in sequence; {place} eats well and marries off its young.
The threshing floors at {place} work past dark. A year to be remembered kindly.
The river moves a ford near {place}. The ferrymen adjust; the maps do not exist to be wrong.
A sandbank closes the old channel at {place}. Boats learn the new one within a season.
The river takes the low fields at {place} and leaves silt as payment.
Flood at {place}; the village rebuilds a little higher, as its grandparents did.
Locusts cross the fields near {place}. What they leave is enough. Barely.
A locust year around {place}; children are sent into the fields with drums.
Lions take cattle near {place}; the herders sit up nights with fire.
A sickness runs through the herds at {place}. The strongest bull is buried, not eaten.
The tank at {place} silts and the assembly argues about whose turn it is to dig.
Desilting at {place}: a month of mud, and water for three more years.
New fields are burned out of the forest near {place}. The ash feeds two harvests.
The clearance line moves a little past {place} this generation.
A chest opened at {place}: worm has taken the outer leaves of a {work} copy.
Damp finds a manuscript of the {work} at {place}. The scribe curses the monsoon and begins again.
Two lineages recite against each other at {place}; a dropped syllable is caught and corrected.
A boy completes the year-long test at {place}. His teacher says nothing, which is praise.
A storyteller works the villages near {place}, paid in meals and barley.
At {place} the storyteller adds a local flood to an old tale. In a century it will be canon.
A student at {place} corrects the teacher, publicly, correctly. An awkward feast follows.
The best student at {place} is sent on — there is nothing more to teach here.
An old reciter dies at {place} with no student ready. What he alone carried goes with him.
The last of a teaching line at {place} is buried. The neighbours cannot say what was lost, which is the loss.
A merchant at {place} pays for a copy of the {work} as merit.
A widow at {place} endows the copying of the {work} in her husband's name.
Two schools at {place} dispute a reading. It takes a decade and settles nothing.
A quarrel over precedence at {place}; the younger school walks out and prospers.
Ploughing near {place} turns up an old inscribed stone. It is set upright and garlanded.
Children find worked stone in a field at {place}. The old people have three explanations.
A caravan is a month late into {place}. Prices say so before the news does.
Word at {place}: the pass held snow into spring. The {good} will be dear this year.
A good market at {place}: {good} moving briskly, and a dispute over weights settled by lunch.
The {good} sellers at {place} agree standard measures. The buyers celebrate cautiously.
A new ferry at {place}; the crossing that took a morning takes an hour.
The ford at {place} gets a rope and a toll. Complaints, and traffic, both rise.
Two trading families of {place} marry their children. The route is now a household matter.
A marriage at {place} settles a debt and opens a road. Cheaper than soldiers.
A weights dispute at {place} goes to the assembly. The offending stone is broken publicly.
A trader at {place} is caught with a hollow weight. His name is remembered longer than his goods.
A boat goes down off {place} with the season's {good}. The sea keeps its accounts privately.
Wreckage at {place}. The insurers — three brothers and an uncle — argue apportionment for a year.
A boundary feud near {place}: two villages, one mango tree, forty years of grievance.
The feud at {place} is settled by oath at the shrine. The tree is declared nobody's.
A wedding at {place} empties three granaries and settles two disputes.
Wedding season at {place}; the drummers are booked a year ahead.
A new well at {place}, dug by subscription. The donors' names are recited, in order, often.
The well at {place} strikes sweet water at forty hands. A feast, and then the argument about turns.
A fever runs through {place} and moves on. The season's work limps.
Sickness at {place}; the shrine is busy and the fields are not.
A weaver at {place} finishes a cloth people walk a day to see.
The potters of {place} fire a batch so fine the buyer pays without haggling. Once.
The shrine at {place} gets a new roof. The carpenter signs a beam where nobody will see.
Repairs at {place}: the old image is carried out, washed, and carried back. The whole village walks with it.
A hero stone is raised near {place} for a man who died turning a cattle raid.
The new hero stone at {place} gets oil and flowers. The raiders' village pretends not to know.
Pilgrims pass through {place} heading for the river. The village sells them everything twice.
A pilgrim party rests at {place} and leaves behind a song nobody here knew.
Grain moves quietly between kin at {place}; nobody calls it what it is.
The headman at {place} opens his pit early. It is remembered at the next election of the committee.
Families from the failed lands settle below {place}. In a generation the accent will be local.
New households at {place}; the assembly grants waste land and watches carefully.
An assessor works the fields near {place}. The measuring rope is checked against the temple's.
Assessment at {place}: three appeals, one granted, all recorded.
The toll at {place} rises; the carters reroute for a season until it quietly falls.
A toll-farmer at {place} overreaches and is replaced. His successor overreaches more slowly.
Levies drill at {place} after harvest. More dust than menace, this year.
The muster at {place}: spears counted, two missing, one goat accepted in lieu.
An order is read aloud at {place}. Half the crowd came for the reading, half for the market after.
A proclamation at {place}; the scribe reads it twice, the second time slower, for the summariser at the back.
